messages:
sam: heads up — noticed a big spike in DCGM exporter ECC/Xid alerts in eu-west1 around 03:10 UTC. A lot of transient card flapping caused a cascade of drains and we lost ~30% GPU capacity in the cluster. proposing a two-part fix: 1) alert rate-limit/suppression at Alertmanager per-card, 2) a staggered-drain playbook to avoid simultaneous drains. anyone see anything I missed?

maya: saw it live — controllers started cordoning nodes, pods OOMed while waiting for reschedules :grimacing:. we had to manually abort two drains.

laura: yeah, noise magnitude was higher than usual. current prometheus rule fires on a single Xid spike + for: 1m which is too aggressive.

ryan: quick note — we've tried simple for: increases before, but the real issue is repeated bursts across cards. need per-card suppression + global grouping guard so Alertmanager doesn't flood pagers and autoscaler.

sam: agreed. draft proposal:
- Prom rule: change to require 3 consecutive 1m windows OR use max_over_time to detect sustained errors. keep shorter detection for oncall dashboard but suppress page.
- Alertmanager: add per-card grouping and a route that sets repeat_interval to 30m and group_interval to 10m for dcgm:* alerts, plus an inhibition rule for node-level drains.
- Staggered drain playbook: small state machine (mark -> cordon -> evict one GPU index -> wait health-check -> proceed to next index) to avoid evicting all GPUs on a host.

laura: example Prom rule tweak:```yaml
- alert: DCGM_ECC_XID_Sustained
  expr: >-
    increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[1m]) > 0
    unless max_over_time(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m]) == 0
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: warning
```
(rough sketch)

ryan: and sample Alertmanager route snippet:```yaml
route:
  receiver: ops-sre
  group_by: ['card_uuid']
  group_interval: 10m
  repeat_interval: 30m
routes:
  - match:
      alertname: 'DCGM_ECC_XID_Sustained'
    receiver: ops-sre
    continue: false
```
This groups by card_uuid so we don't get per-node storms. Also add an inhibit rule: if node is already quarantined/cordoned then suppress further alerts for that node for 1h.

maya: playbook steps I'd run:```text
1) annotate card as investigating: gpu/card_uuid=... -> "investigating"
2) cordon node
3) drain only affected GPU index (use pod-selector or custom evict job)
4) run quick stress test (5m) and free-run workload check
5) if passes -> uncordon and clear annotation
6) if fails -> label 'flaky' and schedule RMA/replace
```
We need automation for step 3 — manual is too slow during bursts.

sam: for automation, propose a controller script using index-aware eviction: `kubectl get pods -l gpu=card_uuid -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl delete --grace-period=60` but gated by a per-host mutex to enforce one GPU at a time. we can package as a small k8s job that accepts `card_uuid` and `max_inflight=1`.

laura: +1. we should also add a short cooloff annotation to nodes we recently drained: `redwood.io/drain-cooloff: '30m'` and have alertmanager inhibition use that label.

ryan: one more idea — for hosted autoscaling, mark pool as 'degraded' and prevent immediate scale-down for 1h so capacity doesn't oscillate.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-44 (DCGM alert storm — eu-west1). Pager duty notified.

maya: rollout plan? small experiment in eu-west1-b canary: enable new route + playbook for 24h, monitor missed detections vs noise.

sam: plan sounds good. can someone pick up codifying the Alertmanager route + Kubernetes eviction job? target PR by EOD tomorrow.

laura: I'll draft the Alertmanager changes and a sample playbook doc.

ryan: I'll prototype the index-aware eviction job and add host mutex logic.

maya: I'll run the canary and own oncall for the window.

sam: perfect. thanks all :thumbsup:
